name: Tevfik Arif

summary.text: Tevfik Arif is a Kazakhstan-born businessman who founded the Bayrock Group, a New York real-estate development and investment firm, in 2001, with offices in Trump Tower, and who with Felix Sater was the firm's principal; Bayrock was the Trump Organization's partner on Trump SoHo. In September 2010 Turkish authorities detained him after a raid on the yacht Savarona and prosecutors charged him in connection with an alleged prostitution ring; he denied the charges, calling them imaginary, and was acquitted of all charges, with sources giving the date as 2011 or 2012. He was a defendant in Kriss v. Bayrock Group (S.D.N.Y. No. 10 Civ. 3959), a RICO suit by a former Bayrock finance director that settled in 2018 without adjudication of its allegations. The Bayrock and Felix Sater files on this site hold the firm's record.

facts.claim: Arif set up the Bayrock Group in New York in 2001, opening an office in Trump Tower two floors below the Trump Organization; the firm described itself as an international real estate development and investment company.

facts.claim: On the night of September 28, 2010 Turkish police raided the yacht Savarona and detained Arif; prosecutors alleged he ran and financed a prostitution ring involving underage girls, with charges including trade in human beings, inducement to prostitution and creation of a criminal organization. Arif denied the charges, calling them imaginary.

facts.claim: A Turkish court acquitted Arif of all charges in the Savarona case; HuffPost, citing The Guardian, dates the acquittal to April 2011, while an Investigate Russia profile gives 2012.

facts.claim: Arif was a defendant in Kriss v. Bayrock Group LLC, S.D.N.Y. No. 10 Civ. 3959, in which former Bayrock finance director Jody Kriss alleged that the Arif/Sater agreement created a RICO enterprise; Bloomberg reported on February 22, 2018 that the firm settled the suit. The allegations were not adjudicated.
